items: 13. On--or CLOSEST TO--the actual length, time, mass, energy, etc SCALES OF BIOCHEMICAL PROCESSES, structures, and units: microbes may naturally have acquired the greatest and most fundamental molecular and physiological sophistication, and may represent the 'consultative plane' of biochemical innovation and interadjustment for all or the larger organisms.
14. May have an ASYMMETRIC PATHOGENIC POWER to devastate or extinguish all larger life, while remaining sublimely invulnerable to the latter.

15. Being CLOSEST TO THE GENETIC, suborganismal, and micro-phenic LEVEL [cf. #12]: may permit or involve the fastest lineal or cross-lineal transfers and interchanges of genetic information, innovations, adaptations, commands, messages, etc.

16. May represent the LEAST SPECIALIZED AND/OR THE MOST GENERALIZED FORM OF LIFE, or the most generalized, primitive, fundamental, persistent, all-important, or all-directive biological (bios) information or universal evolutionary plan; by contrast, larger organisms--and in proportion to their largeness or (supposed) 'level of advancement'--may be excessively or even aberrantly specialized or 'noisy' (dissonant).

17. [BODILY SYSTEMS, organs, tissues, cell types, organelles, biochemical pathways and mechanisms, hormones, large-scale bodily functions, various mechanical, electrical, and chemical devices, sensors, effectors, etc] that are seen IN LARGER ORGANISMS may simply be larger-scale, explicit, specialized, or simplified isomorphic, homomorphic, polygenous, or polymorphic RE-CREATIONS (projections, so to say) OF CONSTANT OR ARCHETYPAL INNOVATIONS BY microbes on the microscopic or ultramicroscopic scale; microbes may SYNTHESIZE AND EMBODY--in REALIZED OR LATENT [unrecognizable, schematic, virtual, or 'ideonomical'] form--whole classes, or a veritable hierarchy or network of taxa of CLASSES, OF such currently or perhaps one day useful INVENTIONS.

18. GENOMES OF all LARGER ORGANISMS may be DYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE over the long term, AND DERIVE such STABILITY as they have FROM periodic or incessant adjustments by or acquisitions or interchanges of genes from or via microbes and/or suborganisms, either because the latter represent by far the larger or combinatorially most various 'gene pool' or because the latter mediate the horizontal gene flow and dynamic unity of the one and irreducible genotype and phenotype that all life on earth--the spatiotemporally indivisible bios--really represents; and conceivably all LARGER--or all--ORGANISMS are 'CONTINUALLY REEVOLVING' FROM the smaller or smallest.

19. Even in a general way [cf. #18], it is NOT CLEAR that MACROORGANISMS should be treated as INDEPENDENT ORGANISMS, or as DIVISIBLE FROM the microbes that may be their multifold symbiotic partners, 'external or shared organelles', or whatever.

20. May be the MOST EFFICIENT organisms in one-or many ways: the acquisition, storage, transmission, use, or transformation of any form or forms of energy, matter, space, etc [incl. the extraction, processing, movement, etc of geochemicals]; locomotion or cellular movement; intracellular operations, biochemical syntheses, transformation or regulation of the external environment; transmission, processing, or storage of various forms of biological information; reproduction or sexuality; [miniaturization, acceleration, combination, multiplexing, modulation, alternation, specialization, standardization, systematization, stabilization, control, stratification, etc] of functions; achievement of redundancy or irredundancy; etc.

21. May be the HEART OF GAIA: in the sense of being that which originated and now maintains, protects, directs, and/or evolves the life-favorable elements and phenomena of the geos [geological, hydrological, and atmospheric].

22. LIFE may mainly or simultaneously be EVOLVING BACKWARDS TOWARD SIMPLICITY OR THE TINIEST forms of matter, or may be predominantly evolving around the eschatological and archological 'black hole' or 'essential singularity' of the genome or chromosomes.

23. FOR BEING THE SIMPLEST organisms or the organisms with the fewest parts or least cumbersome and interfering genomes [or, more esoterically, for being that which is closest to the paradoxically and mysteriously preinfinite and supertemporal apeiron]: MAY BE THE MOST EVOLVED, in general or in special and key ways.
24. May actually have EVOLVED LARGER ORGANISMS: to serve as useful servants, vehicles, tools, habitats, or experiments.

25. It is NOT NECESSARILY true that the smallest organisms--or at least, neontological forms of same--are the MOST ANCIENT or least derivative; larger organisms, or what we call higher organisms, may have come earlier and given rise to at least those tiniest organisms we see around us today, or the latter may be utterly transformed versions or mimics of what were in fact the earliest, most primitive, lowest, or tiniest organisms.

26. 'LARGENESS' OR MULTICELLULARITY--against the near-infinity of other and orthogonal biological dimensions--may be a relatively superficial and even IRRELEVANT trait that is merely conspicuous or anthropocentric; the presently or ultimately most advanced or important evolutionary directions, vectors, or goals may be unrelated, dimensionless, merely additive, or synthetic and even 'holonomical': with respect to size, mass, redundancy (meristic or auxetic), complexity, longevity, or the like.
27. SIMILARLY [vide #26] FOR OTHER ANTHROPOMORPHOUS DIMENSIONS and qualities: not excepting even intelligence or civilization [at least as we ourselves know or are conscious of them].
28. Evolution's thrust and accomplishment may essentially be bipolar and antisyzygial: with LIFE AT ITS SMALLEST as important as, and complementary or even COESSENTIAL TO, LIFE AT ITS BIGGEST.
